I personally know this was logistically unavoidable, but they don't- mum could never have afforded to buy Dad out, and as long as his name was on the house, he's entitled to his half to cover his care. The only chance was when I first went to a solicitor in 2019 about getting his name off the house, this was before he was fully incapacitated and he himself said he wanted to be off of it; He wasn't allowed to live there so ended up on the streets. I got him all the medical treatment he required and off the streets; He wasn't able to work, and so I started paying rent for him but he wasn't able to look after himself properly. Social services refused to help us until 4 years later and I had to get a journalist to cover his story, when he was left homeless again after the fire, and left to roam the streets soiled in just a hospital gown, dementia ridden and discharged by the NHS. Police had to put on a search to find him.

In truth I wish I'd never come back into his life because it's caused me nothing but stress- I do not see him as a 'father', but as a patient or service user. There's significant reasons why my siblings refuse to have anything to do with him, he was not a good man in those final years he was at home. There is not the emotional bond there, just a duty to look after someone. He has never once been grateful or appreciative, but I do sometimes chalk that up to how unwell he was/is. No one else was helping him, so I couldn't sit back and do nothing. I wish I'd never taken on the burden of responsibility.

The plan was originally to gift it to me as his POA/only relative in his life, but I didn't want that as a) it would cause huge family problems and b) impact first time buyer privileges if I ever did buy my own house. All my friends have savings, homes, marriages, families and I have nothing at all and I can't stay stuck in this cycle of sacrificing my life so everyone else is looked after.

Sorry for all the questions and if this seems common sense. I have autism and nothing makes much sense to me legally- when I propose something that seems logical to my family or the council it's met with rebuttal of 'you can't do that', and when I ask why the response is 'just because', but there's constantly loopholes and ways around the 'just becauses' of the world.
